questions.question: Rohit multiplies a number by 2 instead of dividing the number by 2. Resultant number is what percentage of the correct value?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the number be x.

Correct value = x/2

Resultant number = 2 × x

**Calculations:**

According to Question,

Required percentage = Resultant number/Correct value × 100

⇒ Required percentage = [(2x)/(x/2)] × 100

⇒ Required percentage = 400%

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a work in 105 days. Q and R together can complete the same work in 90 days, P and R together can complete the same work in 126 days. In how many days P, Q and R together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Efficiency = 1/Number of days required to complete work

**Calculation:**

Work done by P and Q in 1 day = 1/105

Work done by Q and R in 1 day = 1/90

Work done by R and P in 1 day = 1/126

Adding all of them together

⇒ 2 × (R + P + Q) = 1/105 + 1/90 + 1/126 = (6 + 7 + 5)/630 = 18/630 = 1/35

⇒ R + P + Q = 1/70

∴ R, P and Q can complete the work in 70 days

questions.question: If P : Q : R = 5 : 3 : 6, then what will be the ratio of P/Q : Q/R : R/P?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

P : Q : R = 5 : 3 : 6

Le P be 5x, Q be 3x and R be 6x

Then, (P/Q) ∶ (Q/R) ∶ (R/P) = (5x/3x) ∶ (3x/6x) ∶ (6x/5x)

Let us take the LCM (3, 6, 5) = 30

So, (P/Q) ∶ (Q/R) ∶ (R/P) = (5x/3x) × 30 ∶ (3x/6x) × 30 ∶ (6x/5x) × 30

∴ Required ratio is 50 ∶ 15 ∶ 36

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given: **

P : Q : R = 5 : 3 : 6

Le P be 5x, Q be 3x and R be 6x.

**Concept:**

If N is divided into a : b, then

First part = N × a/(a + b)

Second part = N × b/(a + b)

**Calculations:**

The required ratio = P/Q : Q/R : R/P

Multiplying the above ratio with PQR

⇒ Required ratio = P²R : Q²P : R²Q

Putting values of P,Q and R in above ratio, we get

⇒ Required ratio = (5x)²(6x) : (3x)²(5x) : (6x)²(3x)

⇒ Required ratio = (25x²)(6x) : (9x²)(5x): (36x²)(3x)

⇒ Required ratio = (25)(2) : (3)5: (36)

⇒ Required ratio = 50 : 15 : 36

questions.question: The average weight of a group of 24 students increases by 2 kg when the weight of the teacher is also included. If the initial average weight of the group of 24 students was 30 kg, then what is the weight of the teacher?
questions.solution:
**FORMULA:**

Average = Sum of weight/Number of students

**CALCULATION:**

Suppose, the weight of the teacher = x kg

Average weight of the group = 30 kg

According to Question,

[(24 × 30) + x]/25 = (30 + 2)

[(24 × 30) + x] = 25 × (32)

⇒ x = 80

∴ Weight of the teacher = 80 kg

questions.question: A person purchased 12 bags of sugar at the rate of Rs. 1200 per bag, 8 bags at the rate of Rs. 1500 per bag and 10 bags at the rate of Rs. 2100 per bag. What will be the average cost of all the bags together?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Total number of bags = 30 bags

**CONCEPT:**

When the product is the same but it’s price is different in different batches, then we calculate the weighted Average.

**FORMULA USED:**

Average = Sum of all numbers/Total numbers

Weighted Average = Sum of (number of bags × Average cost of bag)/Total numbers of Bags

**CALCULATION:**

Average cost of 12 bags = Rs. 1200

⇒ Sum of cost of 12 bags = 1200 × 12 = 14400

Average cost of 8 bags = Rs. 1500

⇒ Sum of cost of 8 bags = 1500 × 8 = 12000

Average cost of 10 bags = Rs. 2100

⇒ Sum of cost of 10 bags = 2100 × 10 = 21000

⇒ Sum of cost of 30 Bags = (14400 + 12000 + 21000) = 47400

⇒ Average cost of all 30 Bags = 47400/30 = Rs. 1580

∴ The average cost of all the bags together is Rs. 1580

**Alternate method :**

Weighted Average = [(12 × 1200) + (8 × 1500) + (10 × 2100)]/(12 + 8 + 10)

⇒ Average cost of all 30 Bags = (14400 + 12000 + 21000) /(30)

⇒ Average cost of all 30 Bags = 47400/30 = Rs. 1580

∴ The average cost of all the bags together is Rs. 158

questions.question: The marked price of a chair and a table are in the ratio 2 : 3 respectively. The shopkeeper gives a 20% discount on the chair. If the combined discount on both the chair and the table is 26%, then what will be the discount given on the table?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of a chair and a table are in the ratio 2 : 3.

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Marked Price(100 - Discount)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the discount percentage on table be x.

Ratio of the marked price of a chair and a table = 2 : 3

Marked price of the Chair = Rs 200x

Marked price of the Table = Rs 300x

⇒ Combined price = Rs (200x + 300x) = Rs 500x

Discount = 26%

⇒ Combined selling price = Rs 500x (1 – 26/100) = Rs 370

In 1st case,

⇒ Selling price of chair = Rs 200x (1 – 20/100) = Rs 160

In 2ⁿd case,

⇒ Selling price of table = Rs 300x (1 – x/100) = Rs (300 – 3x)

According to Question,

⇒ Combined selling price = Selling price of chair + Selling price of table

⇒ 370 = 160 + (300 – 3x)

⇒ x = 30%

**∴ The discount given on the table is 30%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** The marked price of a chair and a table are in the ratio 2 : 3

Chair : Table

200 : 300

Total discount = 500 ×26over100 = 130

Discount on the chair = 200 × 20over100 = 40

Discount on the table = 130 - 40 = 90

Percentage discount on the table = 90over300 × 100 = 30%

**∴ The percentage discount on the table is 30%.**

questions.question: If Highest common Factor of two numbers is 8, then which of the following cannot be their Least Common Multiple?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The LCM of any two numbers must always be a multiple of their HCF.

Divide the given options by the HCF (8) to check for exact divisibility.

Options 72, 24, and 48 are completely divisible by 8.

68 is not exactly divisible by 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 68.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of two numbers = 8

**Concept Used:**

Let the two numbers be 8x and 8y, where x and y are co-prime to each other.

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of these numbers will be 8xy.

This shows that the LCM must always be an exact multiple of the HCF.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let's check 72: 72 ÷ 8 = 9 (Exact multiple)

⇒ Let's check 24: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 (Exact multiple)

⇒ Let's check 68: 68 ÷ 8 = 8.5 (Not an exact multiple)

⇒ Let's check 48: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 (Exact multiple)

⇒ Since 68 leaves a remainder when divided by 8, it cannot be the LCM of the two numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 68.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

The product of any two numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (Product = HCF × LCM).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is exactly their product.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators)
LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)
</p

questions.question: If the side of a square increases by 20%, then what will be a percent increase in its perimeter?
questions.solution:

Let the side of the square be x

And Perimeter of square = 4x

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of square = 4 × (side)

Area of Square = (side)²

Area of Circle = π × (radius)² 

Perimeter of Circle = 2 × π × (radius)

**Concept : **

If sides increase by 20%. So Perimeter also increases by 20%

Sides become 1.2 times original

So, Perimeter becomes 4 × 1.2 = 1.2 times original

**Alternative solution:**

Let the side of the square be 100 cm

Side of the square is increased by 20% becomes = 100 + 100 × 20/100

⇒ 120 cm

Perimeter before increase = 4 × 100 = 400 cm

After 20% increased = 4 × 120 = 480 cm

Increase in percentage = [(480 - 400)/400]× 100

⇒ 20%

questions.question: A alone can complete a work in 14 days and B alone can complete the same work in 21 days. A and B start the work together but A leaves the work after 4 days of the starting of work. In how many days B will complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 14 days

B can complete the work in 21 days

**Concept:**

In this type of question always imagine the total work as LCM of time taken by individuals to perform the work.

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be LCM of 21, 14 i.e 42 unit

So, Efficiency of A = 42/14 = 3 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 42/21 = 2 unit/day

Efficiency of (A + B) = 5 unit/day

According to Question,

A and B work for 4 days and performed work = 4 × 5 = 20 unit

Remaining work left = 42 – 20 = 22 unit

B completes the remaining work = 22/2 = 11 days

∴ Time taken by B to complete the remaining work is 11 da

questions.question:
A bowler has taken 0, 3, 2, 1, 5, 3, 4, 5, 5, 2, 2, 0, 0, 1 and 2 wickets in 15 consecutive matches.

What is the median of the given data?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of Matches = 15

**Formula used:**

Median = [(n/2)th + (n/2 + 1)th]/2

Where n is number of terms (even)

Median = [(n + 1/2)th]

Where n is number of terms (odd)

**Calculations:**

First of all we have to arrange the given data in ascending order

0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5

Now,

Median = [(n + 1)/2)th] = 8Th term = 2

∴ The Median of the above data is 2.
